newsitem.title: USA: Demand thins inventory of offshore drilling rigs.
newsitem.headline: Demand thins inventory of offshore drilling rigs.

text.p: Rising demand for offshore drilling rigs left nine operable rigs available for exploration and production worldwide at the turn of the year, executives with Global Marine Inc said on Monday.
"In the whole world, there are nine of them...nine rigs that are physically capable of operating and have a crew," Global Marine Chairman Russell Luigs said.
While the supply of idle rigs thins out, demand continues to rise as producers seek to replace existing reserves and meet growing worldwide demand for oil and gas, he said.
Over the next five years, 90 percent of new supplies will have to come from new wells at a time when global demand rises by an estimated one million barrels per day per year, he said.
"The significance of that is really hard to overstate," Luigs said. "We're going to be looking for nearly another 20 million barrels per day before you know it."
Global Marine's rigs are working under leases averaging 7 months in duration, with 22 of the Houston company's 26 rigs available for new contracts in the coming year, he said.
"We are deliberately trying to remain short in a rising market," Luigs said.
